text:
leah: Hey everyone — first day networking hiccup. I can reach public sites but not our internal docs at http://internal-docs or services on 10.2.0.0/16 from WSL2 on my Windows laptop. Windows browser can reach them when I RDP into a bastion, but curl inside WSL times out. Anyone seen this? :wave:

jamie-it: Welcome! :tada: Sounds like WSL networking is on a different vNIC and not getting the split-route pushed. Can you paste output of `ip addr` inside WSL and `route print` on Windows? Also, which VPN client/agent did you install?

leah: I installed the company OpenVPN package (company-vpn.exe) and it shows connected. WSL `ip addr` shows `eth0` with 172.23.5.4, Windows `route print` shows a 10.2.0.0 route via 172.23.1.1 on `vEthernet (WSL)` though. Quick outputs:
```
# wsl ip addr
eth0: inet 172.23.5.4/20
lo: 127.0.0.1
```
Windows `route print` includes `10.2.0.0    255.255.0.0    172.23.1.1    25`

jamie-it: Huh. Two possibilities: 1) the VPN client is using per-app split routing and traffic from WSL isn't routed through the VPN adapter, or 2) Windows firewall is blocking NAT from WSL to the VPN adapter. Try `wsl --shutdown` then restart WSL and reconnect VPN. If that doesn't work, try adding a manual route inside WSL pointing at the Windows gateway: `sudo ip route add 10.2.0.0/16 via 172.23.1.1 dev eth0` — but that might be temporary.

devops-liz: Quick note: we recently rolled a policy where the VPN only pushes the internal subnet to the primary Windows interface, and WSL's default NAT might not honor it. We prefer using the bastion jumpbox for admin traffic, but for dev workflows you can enable "WSL integration with Windows network" workarounds. If you want a persistent fix, we can create a local static route on the Windows host: `netsh interface ipv4 add route 10.2.0.0/16 "vEthernet (WSL)" 172.23.1.1` — run as admin. That forwards WSL traffic into the VPN.

leah: I ran `wsl --shutdown` and reconnected VPN, still no luck. Tried the `ip route add` in WSL and curl works for a minute then stops. Rebooting Windows is not ideal on day 1 :grimacing:.

alex-eng: @leah if you need quick access to internal docs, you can `ssh -J user@bastion.internal internal-user@internal-docs` or set up an SSH SOCKS proxy: `ssh -D 1080 -J user@bastion.internal user@bastion.internal` and point `curl --socks5-hostname localhost:1080 http://internal-docs`. Not perfect but works without changing system routes.

leah: Thanks, that SOCKS proxy trick worked for docs. Might still need to run services that expect direct IP access though.

devops-liz: We'll open a ticket with IT to evaluate pushing the route into WSL's vNIC more reliably. In the meantime, two options: 1) use the SSH proxy for web/HTTP access, 2) add the netsh route as an admin on your machine (we can approve a ticket), or 3) we can provision a short-lived dedicated dev host inside the VPC for you. Which do you prefer?

leah: SSH proxy for docs is fine for now. If I hit service-level issues I'll request the admin route. Appreciate the quick help! :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Incident/create — channel: new-hires — created ticket IT-4279: "WSL routing to internal VPC for new hire" assigned to jamie-it, priority: low.
